In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data obtained from the experiments described in this thesis indicate that B. cenocepcacia has a complex iron uptake system which can be activated in response to different environmental cues.

the iron acquisition strategies employed by B. cenocepcacia are multifaceted, and that the expression and activity of these systems is modulated in response to iron availability and the presence of competing bacteria.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the expression of iron acquisition systems in B. cenocephalia is complex and dependent on the environment and that B. cenocephaia has a number of iron acquisition systems which are differentially regulated in the presence of iron chelators, other iron acquisition systems and in the course of chronic infection.

the ability of B. cencopacia to utilise haemin, ferritin and transferrin, as well as pyochelin, ornibactins and siderophore-mediated iron uptake, is important for survival in the host environment.
